facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old woman
history of hypertension
stage IA estrogen receptor–positive and progesterone receptor–positive and ERBB/neu receptor–negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast
presented with blurry vision in both eyes
1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to her presentation
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/40 OD and 20/25 OS
Pupils were equal, round, and reactive without an afferent pupillary defect
Intraocular pressures were normal
mild cataracts in both eyes
parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in the right and left eyes
the crystalline deposits did not display autofluorescence
Crystalline deposits located at the level of the outer plexiform layers with some extension into the inner nuclear area subfoveally

concepts.why: The patient's history of anastrozole use and the presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes are consistent with anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of mild cataracts and parafoveal deposits are consistent with age-related macular degeneration.
The patient's history of breast cancer and the presence of blurry vision and parafoveal deposits are consistent with cancer-associated retinopathy.

The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of blurry vision and parafoveal deposits are consistent with diabetic retinopathy, although the patient's diabetes status is not explicitly mentioned.
The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of blurry vision and parafoveal deposits are consistent with hypertensive retinopathy.
The presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes is consistent with crystalline retinopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of mild cataracts and parafoveal deposits are consistent with macular dystrophy.
The patient's age and the presence of mild cataracts and parafoveal deposits are consistent with retinal degeneration.

The patient's history of breast cancer and the presence of crystalline deposits in the retina, as indicated by the best-corrected visual acuity, are consistent with tamoxifen retinopathy, although the patient denied using tamoxifen, the presentation is similar to that of tamoxifen retinopathy.

rationales.F05: Anastrozole is known to cause crystalline maculopathy, which is a rare side effect.
rationales.F10: The presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits is a characteristic feature of crystalline maculopathy.
rationales.F12: The location of the crystalline deposits at the level of the outer plexiform layers with some extension into the inner nuclear area subfoveally is consistent with crystalline maculopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's recent use of anastrozole and the presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes, which did not display autofluorescence, strongly support Anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy.
